claims.basis: Kunos lists the Countach in the historic/classics vehicle set, while independent Assetto Corsa content references identify the included version as the 5000 Quattrovalvole; period Countach drivetrain documentation establishes the five-speed all-synchromesh manual layout.

The documented Countach drivetrain is a five-speed manual. The Countach family drivetrain is explicitly described as all-synchromesh. The documented manual gearbox is a conventional H-pattern manual; no sequential or paddle control is described. The all-synchromesh manual gearbox establishes ordinary clutch use for running upshifts under the project's derivation rules. The period manual drivetrain source documents no electronic cut system. Downshift-only action. The all-synchromesh manual gearbox establishes ordinary clutch use for running downshifts under the project's derivation rules. Modeled only for upshifts. Synchromesh construction makes a rev-match blip optional rather than a gearbox requirement. No automatic-blip system is documented for this period manual car. The hydraulically operated dry clutch is required to launch the manual car from rest. The exact 1988 QV cockpit image shows a continuous circular three-spoke rim; the record remains a 1985-1988 family candidate, so applicability is medium. The fully visible wheel face has no integrated display; the analog instruments are mounted in the dashboard. No wheel-mounted shift-light strip or lamps are visible on the fully exposed wheel face. The photographed rim forms a continuous closed circumference rather than an open-top wheel. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/shift_pattern, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift.
